verdict.rationale: Letta is a stateful-memory agent platform, so memory erasure is a fair axis. However, the evidence never documents deleting a single memory, deleting by entity or user, or full erasure of an agent's memory. Related items cover other things: memory being file-based and "controllable," /doctor audits, and --ephemeral runs that never persist memory in the first place. None of these is an on-demand deletion capability, so they earn no credit.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can delete a user's memories on demand — single memory, per-entity, or full erasure — to satisfy privacy requirements
